pages.text: Watch: Pope Leo rides in helicopter cockpit during Peru trip Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Pope Leo rides in helicopter cockpit during Peru trip Pope Leo XIV shared a cockpit with pilots from the Peruvian Air Force during his tour of Latin America. Sharing the video to social media, the force said having the Pope join its pilots on Saturday was "an honour and an unforgettable memory". On Sunday, the pontiff arrived in Cusco, a southern Andes Mountains city that was once the heart of the Inca empire. There, the Pope visited an ancient Inca fortress, where he said religious traditions could help counter an age marked by "divisions, wounds, mistrust," stressing that faith should unite people and bring them together "in the light of faith and love." The Peruvian leg of his tour holds special significance for the Pope. He not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities. pages.description: Wayne Rooney says he considered taking his own life during his playing days at Manchester United and was "speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up".
pages.text: Wayne Rooney: Ex-Manchester United captain considered taking own life during playing career - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Rooney scored 53 goals in 120 appearances for England By Mandeep Sanghera BBC Sport journalist Published 4 hours ago Warning: This article contains references to suicide Wayne Rooney says he was "contemplating suicide" during his playing days at Manchester United and was "speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up". The former England captain joined United from Everton in 2004 and went on to become the club's record goalscorer, with 253 goals in 559 appearances. But Rooney, speaking with Gabby Logan on the Life at the Midpoint podcast , external , detailed his struggles off the pitch when eldest son Kai, who is now 17, was a baby. "When I was drinking, I would lock myself in my house for two days and just drink," said Rooney, when asked about the lowest point in his life. "This is probably in my best part of my career playing wise." The 41-year-old went on to explain how he "struggled to deal with it all" and, after opening up to his wife Coleen and his mother, knew he "needed help to get through it". "I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with," he added. "I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well. "I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. I just didn't want to be around anyone. Many favorite activities, including gardening, hunting, fishing, traveling, or recreating take place outdoors, and are all greatly affected by temperature, wind, rain, snow, and ice. As these conditions change, what people do outdoors and how they do it has to change as well. This isn’t always easy for Alaskans whose lifestyles depend on the seasons and natural resources. Warmer Winters Early season snow on mountains near Skagway. NPS In both Skagway and Nome, everyone agreed that the winters are getting warmer. In Skagway, this has meant years when there is not enough snow for cross-country skiing or too much rainfall flooding rivers and keeping people from accessing a favorite hunting spot or hiking trail. And in Nome, warmer winters means lake, river and sea ice that is too thin and weak for safe winter travel. Residents of Skagway noted that because their winters are warmer there is now more rain and less snow than there used to be, and a recurring freeze-thaw cycle that creates more icing conditions. Coastal areas typically have mild weather, while the interior has greater seasonal variation in temperature and precipitation. In Nome, yearly precipitation averages about 15 inches, and the average temperature is about 21 o F. Summers average around 50 o F. The first snow dusting of the year can fall as early as August, although heavy snowfall begins in October and will stay on the ground until May. Winter temperatures typically range from -10 to -20 o F, although it can reach as low as -65 o F, with an even lower windchill factor. With these extreme temperatures, the sea ice in the Bering and Chukchi Sea will freeze up around mid-October and remain frozen until breakup in late-May.
